architecture_snapshot.note: F2 moved after the atomic E1 claim: WP710 gained a bounded scheduler core. This receipt re-read that current core before interpretation; architecture credit remains zero.

observations: PSI reports experienced CPU, memory and I/O stall pressure rather than only utilization.
some denotes partial workload stalls; full denotes complete non-idle workload stalls for memory/I/O and is a severe-thrashing signal.
avg10/avg60/avg300 expose trends while total exposes cumulative stall microseconds.
Userspace can register threshold/window triggers and wait with poll/select/epoll; documented windows are 500 ms to 10 s.
PSI is explicitly intended to support dynamic load shedding and pausing/killing lower-priority work under pressure.
The same PSI interface is available per cgroup v2.
cgroup v2 exposes cpu.pressure, memory.pressure and io.pressure for group-local pressure accounting.
memory.high is a throttle boundary intended to give an external management agent time to react before OOM-style failure.
These are host-control mechanisms; importing them into the pure WP710 scheduler would violate its hardware-independent boundary.
Catan treats sense-react scheduling as a runtime resource-allocation problem over sensing/perception/planning/reaction pipelines.
It keeps application semantic requirements static while adapting low-level execution rates and CPU allocations to observed computation time and resource availability.
This supports separating F2 semantic value/priority policy from host-specific resource-pressure measurement.
Brownout handles overload by temporarily deactivating optional components rather than failing the whole application.
The transferable principle is graceful optional-work degradation under overload; its cloud energy numbers do not transfer to F2.

current_f2_observations: WP710 is explicitly pure/deterministic and may not open devices or grant world/effect/completion authority.
The current scheduler already preserves a caller-declared control_reserve_units and derives pressure_degraded only from available_compute_units <= control_reserve_units.
The current policy has pressure_drop_below_priority_micros, so the architecture already has a deterministic low-value shedding hook but no typed host pressure measurement in this source surface.
hypothesis: A typed host ResourcePressureSnapshot derived outside WP710 from PSI/cgroup-v2 signals can give the scheduler earlier, workload-impact-oriented degradation evidence than raw CPU/RSS utilization, while WP710 remains a pure deterministic planner.
counterhypothesis: available_compute_units plus control_reserve_units already encode sufficient pressure; PSI adds host-specific noise, unrelated-workload coupling and complexity without improving protection of cognition/control.
source_read_conclusion: PROMOTE_TO_E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPING; DO_NOT_IMPORT_KERNEL_OR_CATAN_CODE; prefer a thin F2-native typed pressure adapter and deterministic degradation mapping if later evidence supports it.

candidate_architecture_shape.host_adapter: Read system or dedicated-perception-cgroup PSI and emit an immutable typed ResourcePressureSnapshot with timestamp/generation/provenance.
candidate_architecture_shape.scheduler: Consume only the typed snapshot plus existing available_compute_units/control_reserve_units; never read /proc or cgroupfs directly.
candidate_architecture_shape.degradation: Map pressure to explicit bounded levels that lower worker/work budgets and shed optional low-priority perception before touching the control reserve.
candidate_architecture_shape.anti_flap: Use deterministic hysteresis/dwell rules because PSI threshold notifications and load can oscillate.
candidate_architecture_shape.fallback: If pressure telemetry is missing/stale/unsupported, retain the current compute-envelope path and mark pressure evidence UNKNOWN rather than fabricating NORMAL.

next_exact_gate: Acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED claim, map typed pressure input against current WP710/WP709/Cognitive Envelope boundaries, and specify a falsifiable no-import architecture delta before any Trigger-4 handoff.
